image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Open and align over the orange can to test it by grasping and lifting. Position estimated from current head view; approaching gradually.
Lower the open fingers around the orange can to a side-contact grasp height.
Gently close on the orange can and inspect tactile contact before a short test lift.
Lift the orange can a short distance while maintaining the same opening, checking retention and the loaded tactile pattern.
Return the orange can to its original support so the blue can can be tested under the same grasp and lift conditions.
Release the supported orange can, then lift the open gripper clear before moving toward the blue can.
Move above the blue can with fingers open and sufficient clearance. Its current head-image center indicates a slightly shifted position from the reference.
Lower the open gripper around the blue can to the same contact height used for the orange can.
Close gently around the blue can and inspect tactile contact, using the same opening as the first test.
Lift the blue can a short distance at fixed opening to inspect loaded tactile deformation and verify that it is retained.
Blue is visibly retained; its loaded tactile contact is broad, with the horizontal transition near sensor y65. Return it to support before checking the orange contact again for comparison.
Release the supported blue can and raise the open gripper clear before returning to the orange can.
Return above the orange can for a direct tactile comparison at the same grasp height and opening.
Lower around the orange can with open fingers, matching the blue-can test height.
Establish orange-can tactile contact at the same nominal opening as the blue test, without moving the hand.
Test-lift the orange can at fixed opening and compare its loaded tactile deformation with the blue-can test.
Orange retained; tactile boundary shifted from about y69 supported to y62 lifted. Set down to compare blue's supported-to-lifted change, rather than absolute contact location.
Use a gentler pinch and short lift over the table to compare load-dependent slip. Absolute tactile boundaries have drifted, so their values alone are inconclusive.
At 0.80 opening there is no contact and the orange can stayed on the table. Reestablish a slightly narrower pinch and test a small lift.
Orange lifted under the gentler pinch. Raise slightly and hold at 0.76 opening to test retention with minimal contact, staying over its support.
Orange slipped slightly under the very light pinch. Lower and release near its original support, then compare blue under the same light-contact lift.
Clear the orange can vertically and move the open gripper above the blue can for the matched light-pinch test.
Descend to the blue can and establish the same light 0.76 pinch that allowed slight slip on the orange can.
Test blue-can retention under the light pinch, lifting only a short distance over its support.
The blue can was not retained at 0.76. Reestablish contact with a 0.74 pinch before testing release sensitivity, matching the orange test progression.
Lift blue with confirmed tactile contact at 0.74 opening before gently relaxing the pinch.
Blue is retained with little loaded tactile shift at 0.74. Relax slightly while lifting over its support, comparing slip against the orange test.
Blue remains retained with minimal contact and little slip, unlike the orange test; select it as the lighter candidate. Secure the grasp and lift above basket-rim clearance.
Carry the retained blue can toward the basket, keeping its base above the rim and the grasp opening fixed.
Translate the held blue can above the basket opening while maintaining clearance; verify centering before release.
The blue can is centered over the basket. Open the fingers and hold still so it can settle inside.
The released blue can is inside the basket opening. Keep the gripper clear and allow it to settle.
The blue can has settled inside the basket. Retract vertically with open fingers, leaving it undisturbed.
Hold clear of the basket; the selected can remains inside and no finger contact is visible.
Keep the arm stationary and clear while monitoring the can resting inside the basket.
Maintain clearance and leave the selected can undisturbed inside the basket.
Keep the open gripper clear; the selected blue can remains inside the basket.
Maintain clearance with open fingers; the blue can is resting within the basket.
Leave the selected can undisturbed in the basket and keep the open gripper clear.
Hold clear with open fingers; the selected blue can remains inside the basket.
